images.caption: Figure 1:Robot execution and human interaction in a changing world.(1)Spatially grounded NPC communication depends on human availability and interaction range.(2)Policy-driven grasping uses contact feedback to verify a successful hold.(3)Evolving task requirements, such as recipient changes, trigger replanning.(4)Physical motion is governed by contact, friction, and balance, making collisions and falls part of execution evaluation.

Figure 2:TARSphere-Infra: execution infrastructure.(a)Physics runtime executes robot actions under contact and friction.(b)An event-driven FSM coordinates NPC actions, message delivery, and task-state transitions.(c)Evaluation checks execution evidence against the task requirements active when that evidence was produced.

Figure 3:TARSphere-Harness: the embodied brain harness.(a)Current observations and(b)hierarchical memory inform(c)MLLM decisions.(d)The unified skill interface routes actions to(e)controller backends.(f)Observations, execution feedback, and public world events close the loop.

Figure 4:Agent-in-the-loop curation of TARSphere-Bench.(a)Task, NPC, and scene inputs.(b)Code-as-curator synthesis with joint semantic, causal, and spatial solving.(c)Agent and human review withSKILL.mdrefinement.(d)Simulation validation of task transitions and execution.

Figure 5:TARSphere-Bench statistics.(a)Base and five conditions across 360 episodes.(b)Difficulty of 60 Base tasks with a kernel density estimate.(c)Human exchanges per episode, including the opening; last column: mean.(d)Top 100 terms from 240 distinct opening utterances.

Figure 7:Qualitative comparison of four models on the same task.Egocentric views, reasoning excerpts, and event-triggered causal milestones contrast successful reporting, recovery failure, wrong-person interaction, and unsupported completion claims.
